This 2017 Chevrolet Corvette Z06 is an exceptionally significant example of the C7-generation Z06, carrying VIN 1G1YU2D61H VIN 00001. Believed to be the first C7 Corvette Z06 equipped with the Z07 Performance Package, this car combines unusual production provenance with one of the most desirable performance configurations offered during the C7 era. It is further equipped with the 3LZ Premium Equipment Group, making for an outstanding combination of performance, equipment, and collectibility.



Finished in its factory Arctic White over a Jet Black interior, the Corvette has a striking appearance accented by black and exposed-carbon-fiber components. A removable Arctic White targa roof panel provides open-air driving while maintaining the coupe's distinctive profile. The aggressive Z07 aerodynamic treatment, prominent rear spoiler, functional cooling openings, and carbon-fiber hood section further distinguish the car's performance-focused appearance.



Power comes from Chevrolet's supercharged 6.2-liter LT4 V8, factory rated at 650 horsepower and 650 lb-ft of torque, paired with the 8-speed automatic transmission. The Z07 Performance Package takes the already formidable Z06 platform a step further with its more aggressive suspension calibration and massive carbon-ceramic brakes, creating one of the most capable factory performance packages Chevrolet had produced to that point.



A set of aftermarket Cray forged chrome wheels gives this Z06 a distinctive look while retaining an appropriately aggressive stance. They are wrapped in wide performance tires measuring 285/30R19 up front and 335/25R20 at the rear, filling out the Z06's widened bodywork and providing the substantial footprint expected from a car with this level of performance.

Inside, the 3LZ cabin combines the Z06's performance-oriented layout with the highest level of interior appointments offered for the model. Particularly desirable are the Competition Sport seats with carbon-fiber shells, providing additional lateral support while adding another visible performance element to the cabin. Carbon-fiber interior trim, an Alcantara-wrapped steering wheel, driver-focused controls, and the C7's configurable digital instrumentation complete the cockpit.



What truly separates this Corvette from a typical Z06, however, is its production significance. The VIN ends in 00001, and the car is believed to represent the first C7 Z06 Z07 produced. That provenance, combined with its 3LZ specification, Z07 Performance Package, carbon-ceramic brakes, Competition Sport seats, Arctic White finish, Cray forged wheels, and 650-horsepower supercharged LT4, makes this a particularly compelling example for the Corvette enthusiast or collector seeking something far more unusual than a standard C7 Z06.

This 2013 Chevrolet Corvette 60th Anniversary Coupe combines low mileage with a substantial list of performance upgrades. Finished in Blade Silver Metallic over an Ebony leather interior, the car shows just 14,500 miles and presents as a sharp, heavily upgraded example of the final-year C6 Corvette.



Under the hood is Chevrolet's 6.2-liter LS3 V8, upgraded with a Whipple supercharger and supporting modifications. Additional performance equipment includes a Texas Speed camshaft and valve springs, MSD fuel pump controller, Billy Boat long-tube headers, high-flow catalytic converters, and a stainless-steel dual exhaust system. The combination is rated at approximately 600 horsepower while retaining the usability of the factory six-speed automatic transmission and limited-slip differential. A supplied dyno sheet documents 583.46 horsepower and 510.28 lb-ft of torque at the wheels.



Stopping performance has also been upgraded with Wilwood four-wheel disc brakes, visible behind the staggered 19-inch front and 20-inch rear American Racing wheels. The rear wheels are now wrapped in 275-series Nitto NT555 tires, providing a performance-oriented setup to complement the added power. A fiberglass scooped hood adds a more purposeful appearance while providing clearance for the Whipple supercharger.



The Blade Silver Metallic exterior maintains the clean lines of the C6 while incorporating several tasteful updates. Upgraded headlights and taillights modernize the appearance, while the removable translucent targa roof panel provides the option of open-air driving without giving up the profile of the coupe. The combination of the silver finish, dark wheels, and red brake calipers gives the car a restrained but unmistakably performance-oriented appearance.



Inside, the Corvette retains its Ebony leather cabin and factory-oriented layout. A Kenwood touchscreen infotainment system has been added along with front and rear cameras, bringing useful modern technology to the C6 interior. The removable roof panel can be stored for open-air driving, adding another dimension to an already versatile performance car.



With approximately 600 horsepower, Whipple-supercharged LS3 power, a Texas Speed cam, long-tube exhaust, upgraded Wilwood brakes, staggered American Racing wheels, translucent targa roof, upgraded lighting, and just 14,500 miles, this 2013 Corvette offers an impressive combination of C6 styling, serious performance, and everyday drivability.

description:
This one-owner 2023 Dodge Charger SXT AWD Blacktop Special Edition arrives dressed to intimidate in rare B5 Blue, a color that turns heads in daylight and looks even meaner after dark. The factory Blacktop treatment wraps the stance in gloss-black grille and crosshairs, satin-black Dodge and Charger badges, a black AWD rhombi badge, a one-piece performance spoiler, and twenty-inch Black Noise AWD wheels wearing all-season performance rubber, so the four-door muscle car reads like a purpose-built street machine instead of a family sedan. Dual bright exhaust tips and LED projector headlamps with daytime running lamps and front fog lamps finish the look, while the Last Call underhood plaque marks this as one of the final Chargers built before the nameplate went out of production.

Under the hood the 3.6-liter Pentastar V6 delivers 300 horsepower through an eight-speed automatic and an intelligent all-wheel-drive system with an active transfer case and front-axle disconnect, giving you year-round grip without constantly dragging extra hardware. Sport mode, performance brakes, and Dodge Performance Pages let you lean into the chassis when the road opens up, yet remote start, push-button ignition, and a composed highway ride keep everyday miles easy.

Slide inside and the cabin matches the attitude: black Houndstooth cloth sport seats, real carbon-fiber interior accents, a leather-wrapped steering wheel with mounted audio controls, and a tilt-and-telescope column. The eight-way power driver s seat with two-way lumbar support, a 60/40 folding rear bench, and a media hub with dual USB plus auxiliary keep the interior practical. Overhead, a power sunroof floods the cabin with light. The Uconnect 4C NAV 8.4-inch touchscreen brings GPS navigation, Apple CarPlay, Android Auto, integrated voice command, a 4G LTE Wi-Fi hotspot, and SiriusXM with Travel Link and Traffic Plus, while six premium Alpine speakers and a 276-watt amplifier fill the car with sound.

Safety and convenience are built in at every corner: ParkSense rear park-assist, a ParkView backup camera, electronic stability control, a full suite of advanced air bags and active head restraints, tire-pressure monitoring, and Sentry Key theft deterrent. This Charger earned a five-star overall NHTSA safety rating, and it still carries the backing of Dodge s five-year/60,000-mile powertrain warranty from new.

One-owner history, loaded Blacktop Special Edition equipment, AWD confidence, and that unmistakable Charger presence make this a last-call muscle sedan that still looks ready to leave the lot like it just rolled off the Brampton line.

description:
Discover the 2025 Nissan Pathfinder SV, a three-row SUV engineered to meet the demands of families and active drivers who need space, capability, and comfort in one package.

- 3.5L V6 engine with 9-speed automatic transmission and 4WD capability
- Three-row seating with split folding rear seats and reclining third row
- Heated front bucket seats with power adjustments
- NissanConnect featuring Apple CarPlay and Android Auto integration
- Front dual-zone automatic temperature control with rear air conditioning
- Rear parking sensors for added convenience during maneuvering
- Remote keyless entry with power liftgate for easy access
- Four-wheel independent suspension with electronic stability control
- All-terrain 18-inch painted alloy wheels
- Leather steering wheel with telescope and tilt adjustment
- SiriusXM satellite radio with six-speaker audio system
- Comprehensive airbag system including front, side, overhead, and knee airbags
- Auto high-beam headlights with delay-off feature

The Pathfinder's three-row configuration provides seating for up to eight passengers, making it an excellent choice for growing families. The split folding rear seats and reclining third row offer flexibility to balance passenger comfort with cargo space as your needs change. Whether you're transporting a full group or maximizing cargo capacity, this layout adapts to your lifestyle.

The real-world efficiency of this V6 delivers 21 miles per gallon in the city and 27 on the highway, balancing power with reasonable fuel economy for regular driving and longer trips. The 4WD system ensures you maintain control in various weather and road conditions throughout the year.

Inside, the Pathfinder SV surrounds you with thoughtful conveniences. Heated front seats keep you warm during cold mornings, while the dual-zone automatic climate control ensures all passengers find their comfort level. The leather steering wheel and adjustable steering column accommodate drivers of different sizes, and the overhead console provides organized storage for essentials.

Modern connectivity comes standard with NissanConnect, seamlessly integrating Apple CarPlay and Android Auto so your smartphone becomes an extension of the vehicle's infotainment system. Steering wheel-mounted audio controls keep your focus on the road while you manage your music and calls safely.

Safety is prioritized throughout the design with a comprehensive airbag system, electronic stability control, traction control, four-wheel independent suspension, and rear parking sensors. These systems work together to help protect your family and provide confidence behind the wheel.

The Silver exterior, accented by heated power mirrors and body-color bumpers, presents a polished appearance whether you're heading to the office or the trailhead. This Pathfinder is ready to handle whatever your day brings.

This vehicle is located at our Indianapolis facility - 2461 Reeves Rd #194, Plainfield, IN 46168



This 1989 GMC S-15 Jimmy is a well-preserved example of GMC's compact two-door SUV, finished in red over a gray and black interior. With its short wheelbase, two-door body, factory-style alloy wheels, roof rack, running boards, and classic GMC styling, this Jimmy has the unmistakable late-1980s look that has become increasingly difficult to find in clean, largely stock form.



Power comes from the 4.3-liter V6 paired with an automatic transmission and four-wheel drive. Power steering, power brakes, front disc brakes, heat, and air conditioning add to its usability. The CARFAX shows 77,329 miles and reports no accidents or damage, no structural damage, and no indication of an odometer rollback. The mileage history is also consistent, progressing from 60,000 miles in 1998 to 75,000 miles in 2006 and 77,329 miles when it was purchased in Indiana in 2021.



According to the previous owner, the Jimmy was purchased in Wisconsin approximately five years ago and was initially used as a daily driver before seeing more limited use. During that ownership, a number of maintenance items and updates were completed. These include replacement of the air-conditioning system around the time of purchase, along with a newer alternator, gas tank, fuel pump, fuel lines, tires, brakes, battery, and a full tune-up. It also received a new fuel-mix switch, radio system, and temperature switch.



The exterior retains a clean, straightforward presentation in red, complemented by black lower trim, GMC badging, a hood deflector, roof rack, running boards, mud flaps, and alloy wheels wrapped in all-terrain tires. The compact two-door proportions give the Jimmy a distinctive appearance compared with today's larger SUVs, while the four-wheel-drive system makes it a practical choice for year-round use.



Inside, the cabin remains appropriately period-correct with gray cloth bucket seats with black trim, a center console, factory-style instrumentation, and an automatic column shifter. An updated audio system provides a useful modern touch without substantially changing the vintage character of the interior.



Underneath, the Jimmy presents as an honest older SUV, showing the type of age and surface corrosion expected from a vehicle that spent much of its life in Wisconsin and the Midwest. The CARFAX documents Wisconsin history dating back to 1990 before the vehicle was purchased and titled in Indiana in 2021. Overall, this 1989 GMC S-15 Jimmy offers a hard-to-find combination of two-door styling, 4.3-liter V6 power, four-wheel drive, relatively low indicated mileage, and a largely stock presentation.

This 1996 Mercury Tracer wagon is a remarkably well-preserved example of an increasingly uncommon piece of 1990s automotive history. Finished in Bright Calypso Metallic over a gray cloth interior, this Tracer has remained with the same owner since new and shows just 55,229 miles. It has spent its life in Indiana as a personal vehicle and averaged only approximately 2,098 miles per year.



Power comes from a 1.9-liter four-cylinder engine paired with an automatic transmission and front-wheel drive. Rated at approximately 88 horsepower when new, the Tracer was designed around simple, economical, and dependable transportation. This example is equipped with power steering, power brakes, front disc brakes, air conditioning, heat, power windows, and power door locks. According to the previous owner, all options operate as they should.



The exterior retains a wonderfully period-correct appearance, with the Bright Calypso Metallic finish giving the wagon the unmistakable teal color associated with the 1990s. Factory-style wheel covers, black window trim, roof rails, and its clean, straightforward body lines complete the look. The wagon body provides considerably more cargo space than the Tracer sedan while retaining compact dimensions that make it easy to drive and maneuver.



Inside, the gray cloth interior remains impressively original in appearance. The cabin features cloth seating, an analog gauge cluster, factory audio system, automatic floor shifter, and straightforward controls throughout. Power windows and power door locks add convenience, while the rear seating and large cargo area provide the everyday practicality expected from a compact station wagon.



Its ownership history is particularly noteworthy. The vehicle was purchased new in Indiana in May 1996 and remained with its original owner for approximately 30 years. The vehicle history shows consistent Indiana registration with no reported accidents, structural damage, total loss, or odometer issues. Service history includes an air filter, evaporative emissions purge valve, evaporator drain hose, and exhaust pipe service in 2019, along with an oil and filter change later that year. The air-conditioning system was recharged in 2022.





For anyone who remembers seeing these cars on the road when they were new, this Tracer offers a genuine dose of 1990s nostalgia. With its one-owner history, actual low mileage, highly original presentation, distinctive Bright Calypso Metallic finish, and the practicality of a four-door wagon, this 1996 Mercury Tracer represents the kind of everyday car that has become surprisingly difficult to find in this condition nearly three decades later.
